subject: Clarifying invoice OCR outputs and BAA scope for attachments
messages:
From: Arup Banerjee <arup@medinvoice.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice OCR and PHI — sample data for BAA scope?

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the call earlier. To speed up our BAA on-boarding evaluation I wanted to confirm what counts as PHI for Redwood's hosted API when customers upload invoice PDFs that include patient names, dates of service, and limited diagnosis codes. A few specific asks:

- If we send invoice attachments (PDF scans) to the hosted API for OCR and line-item extraction, does Redwood classify the raw attachment content as PHI in scope of the BAA?
- Are OCR outputs (plain text or CSV) treated the same as original attachments? If we strip name fields before sending, is that sufficient?
- For sharing sample invoices with your security team, what redaction approach do you prefer and is there a secure upload link we should use?

I've attached two samples (one redacted). Happy to share more. We're trying to determine whether we need a Dedicated or Private deployment for this workload.

Thanks,
Arup
Senior Integrations Lead
MedInvoice
Attachments: invoice_sample_medical_001.pdf (pdf, 220KB), invoice_sample_redacted.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Arup Banerjee <arup@medinvoice.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice OCR and PHI — sample data for BAA scope?

Hi Arup — thanks for sending these and for the clear list of questions. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, if an invoice contains identifiers (names, MRN, dates tied to an individual) we treat that content as PHI in scope of a BAA when processed by our hosted inference API.
- OCR outputs are considered derived PHI; redaction before upload reduces scope but depends on what you remove. Removing direct identifiers (name, DOB, MRN) typically helps; pseudonymization of names also reduces risk but might still be in scope for downstream processing.
- We prefer samples with direct identifiers redacted and a small separately uploaded mapping file (kept only for repro) if you need us to reproduce results. We can also accept fully redacted PDFs and a synthetic sample with similar structure.

Looping in Dev (cc) for technical options (DLP hooks, client-side redaction libraries, and possible Dedicated routing). Dev — can you share the secure upload link and quick notes on retention/scopes and whether OCR outputs are logged in plaintext in our logs?

Best,
Logan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Arup Banerjee <arup@medinvoice.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice OCR and PHI — sample data for BAA scope?

Arup — thanks. Short technical summary from infra/privacy side:

- In hosted mode, attachments sent to the API are written to ephemeral object storage during processing and are available to the inference workers. They are encrypted at rest and in transit. By default we retain artifacts (incoming files, OCR outputs) for 24 hours for debugging; retention can be shortened or disabled under contract (BAA/Dedicated).
- OCR outputs are materialized as plaintext tokens in our processing pipeline and therefore are treated as PHI. They are included in traces used for debugging unless obfuscated.
- Options we recommend:
  1) Client-side redaction: remove names/DOB/MRN prior to upload (preferred). Provide a small synthetic mapping if you need results mapped back.
  2) Use our Dedicated capacity or Private deployment: eliminates multi-tenant hosted retention and allows contractually enforced zero retention and custom logging policies.
  3) Use tokenization proxy: we can route requests through a tokenization service that replaces identifiers with stable pseudonyms before they reach the model.

Secure upload link (S3 pre-signed): https://s3.redwood.example/medinvoice-samples?token=EXAMPLE (expires 48h). Please upload redacted + one raw sample if you have DPA in place; otherwise only redacted.

Naomi — can you confirm whether a 24-hour default retention and evidence (S3 access logs, object metadata) is acceptable as SOC2 evidence for the customer's security team?

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redacted_invoice_ocr.csv (csv, 45KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Arup Banerjee <arup@medinvoice.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice OCR and PHI — sample data for BAA scope?

Hi Arup — quick compliance note:

- Confirming Dev's note: any plaintext OCR outputs are in-scope for PHI under the BAA. If MedInvoice requires hosted processing with raw PHI, we'll need to include that in the BAA scope and contractually agree on retention, logging, and access controls.
- For SOC 2/SIG evidence we can provide:
  - S3 access logs showing object write/delete events
  - Redaction checklists and client-side guidance materials we provided
  - SOC 2 Type II report excerpt (shared under NDA) and relevant CIS/ISO mappings
- If you'd like an on-record assurance, we can schedule a brief evidence call (30 minutes) next week to walk through the artifacts.

Please confirm whether you'll upload a raw sample under existing NDA or only redacted samples.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Arup Banerjee <arup@medinvoice.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Invoice OCR and PHI — sample data for BAA scope?

Hi Naomi/Logan/Dev — thanks for the clarity. We'll take the following next steps:

- We'll upload one raw invoice sample to the provided pre-signed link within 24h under our current NDA. If you confirm retention is limited to 24h and artifacts will be deleted after that window, we can proceed.
- We'll also generate a fully redacted set and a synthetic dataset for you to run benchmarking without sensitive data.
- Please send a calendar invite for the evidence call — afternoons PST work best for our team.

One operational question: can you confirm whether automatic OCR output logging is disabled for Dedicated customers by default, or is that a configuration we must request during onboarding?

Best regards,
Arup
Senior Integrations Lead
MedInvoice
